content: I got through making a v4.29 bump mostly ok, but there's a Stack overflow running on CI with the defineLaws% command. Frustratingly, it runs fine locally. :upside_down: @Joachim Breitner, I think you wrote that code, would you have an idea how to diagnose/improve this?

Hi, the file ForMathlib/ReducedWords.lean is now completely upstreamed, but the API has changed a bit, in particular, Mathlib/GroupTheory/FreeGroup/CyclicallyReduced.lean now defines a IsMulTorsionFree instance for free groups. We should be able to remove the file, I can probably do it over the weekend, but feel free to give it a shot first.

Ah, good to know! Looking at the two files (in our equational_theories, and Mathlib), they look different enough that I think I would make a proper mess trying to adapt it. If you could try to over the weekend, that would be great! Certainly I'm in no rush.

Fixed the stack overflow, just had to pass in a tstack flag with a bigger size. Now it's stuck because the CI looks for lean4checker which, I guess as of a month ago, is deprecated now? I'll be honest, I have no idea where that is controlled or how to fix it. @Kim Morrison I hope it's alright if I ask you for a pointer here. :)
The Github Action calls lean4checker here. Maybe it would work just to delete the part where the checker is downloaded and built?
Ah, thank you for pointing me there. Okay, I tried a fix, let's see.
And just call it as leanchecker, it comes with Lean now

Deleting these lines should suffice for now
https://github.com/teorth/equational_theories/blob/da52e3a6283203a7d5d7765a919b5cbd84437d2e/.github/workflows/blueprint-paper.yml#L112

Hmm, this change seemed reasonable, and indeed it launched and crunched for like an hour and a half, but then the CI run just died during the leanchecker stage. I wonder if it was choking in a manner similar to that stackoverflow.
When I tried running leanchecker like that locally on my projects, it immediately consumed a huge amount of memory and died.

Lean is going to need major updates to handle the math that's coming in the next couple years (maybe months?). I've already had to write sharding algorithms for the output of my drat to lean pipeline to keep the builds running in an acceptable amount of time. Some of our generated lean files were 200,000+ lines.
(and that was just for d=8. higher d values will increase exponentially)

Adam McKenna said:

Lean is going to need major updates to handle the math that's coming in the next couple years (maybe months?). I've already had to write sharding algorithms for the output of my drat to lean pipeline to keep the builds running in an acceptable amount of time. Some of our generated lean files were 200,000+ lines.

Translating a DRAT file to a syntax level Lean term is not a good idea in general. You should instead operate like bv_decide does and translate it to an expression directly which is going to be orders of magnitude faster.
Yes, I've begun to realize that :D. Thanks for the tip on bv_decide.
bv_decide is able to cope with gigabytes of LRAT that contains several hundred thousand proof steps in seconds, there is really no fundamental limitation that's holding you back here.

Alright, I've tried just disabling leanchecker entirely. We'll if the build passes now. If someone is keenly motivated to identify how to make it work again, that would be fantastic, but for now... [shrug]?

David Renshaw said:

When I tried running leanchecker like that locally on my projects, it immediately consumed a huge amount of memory and died.

I'm not shocked, I've heard it's expensive. But I don't really understand why the demands would be so much greater now than a year ago (as opposed to, well, a modest increase for Mathlib increasing, but I don't think that was it.)

Alex Meiburg said:

Ah, good to know! Looking at the two files (in our equational_theories, and Mathlib), they look different enough that I think I would make a proper mess trying to adapt it. If you could try to over the weekend, that would be great! Certainly I'm in no rush.

I had a go, I opened a PR to your bumping branch. Let me know if I missed something or if there are any questions! Some of the files I touched had errors, then I also tried to remove them, but I didn't really do any linting.
